deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft of the end of §11 and of §12 of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (written 1853/54, published posthumously 1867). It is written on the back of, or near, a letter dated Feb. 1853.

(a) Tail of §11. The page finishes the hypotheses of the preceding theorem. The quantity b is a (small) constant. ρ(t) is an auxiliary weight function with these properties:
- ρ and ρ' are continuous and vanish at t=b.
- ρ'' does not have infinitely many maxima and minima.
- ρ(0)=ρ'(0)=ρ''(0)=0.
- ρ''' and ρ'''' are finite and continuous.
The convergence of Ω at x is then decided by whether (2/π)∫_0^b G(t) ∂²/∂t²[sin((2n+1)t/2)/sin(t/2)] ρ(t) dt → 0. Here G(t)=F(x+t)+F(x−t), where F is the twice-integrated (Riemann) function of the series.

(b) §12, first remark. The condition ρ''(0)=0 may be dropped if G(t) is replaced by G(t)−G(0).
- Reason (my fill-in): write D_n(t)=sin((2n+1)t/2)/sin(t/2). It is even, so D_n'(0)=0.
- Integrate by parts twice. All boundary terms vanish because ρ(0)=ρ'(0)=0 and ρ(b)=ρ'(b)=0. This gives ∫_0^b D_n'' ρ dt = ∫_0^b D_n ρ'' dt.
- By Dirichlet, ∫_0^b D_n ρ'' dt → π ρ''(0).
- So the constant part G(0) contributes (2/π)·G(0)·π ρ''(0) = 2G(0)ρ''(0) in the limit. This term is removed either by assuming ρ''(0)=0 or by subtracting G(0).
- Riemann adds that 'nothing essential is gained' by this.

(c) Turn to special cases: functions without infinitely many maxima and minima, completing Dirichlet's work.
- Such an f is integrable wherever it is finite. Points where it is infinite can only be finitely many.
- Dirichlet's proof already shows the following for ∫ f(t) sin((2n+1)(x−t)/2)/sin((x−t)/2) dt (the n-th term and the n-th partial sum, up to a factor 1/2π):
  - contributions from all stretches except those near infinities of f and near t=x tend to 0;
  - ∫_x^{x+b} f(t) D_n(x−t) dt → π f(x+0) for 0<b<π, if f is finite there.
- This holds without the 'superfluous' (margin: 'unnecessary') continuity hypothesis.
- What remains is when the contribution of the singular points tends to 0. Dirichlet showed this only incidentally, assuming the function admits an integration (integrability near the singularities). Riemann says this assumption is not necessary.

(d) Start of the necessary-condition argument.
- From earlier sections: if the terms of Ω tend to 0 for every x, then F (with F''=f) is finite and continuous, and [F(x+α)−2F(x)+F(x−α)]/α → 0. This is Riemann's second lemma.
- If F'(x+t)−F'(x−t) has finitely many maxima and minima, it must tend to a limit or to ∞ as t→0.
- The next page continues with the identity (1/α)∫_0^α (F'(x+t)−F'(x−t)) dt = [F(x+α)−2F(x)+F(x−α)]/α. This forces that limit to be 0.
- It ends in the published necessary and sufficient condition: at a singular point a, t·f(a±t) → 0 and f(a+t)+f(a−t) is integrable up to t=0.
errors: No mathematical error on this page itself. The claim that the ρ''(0)=0 condition can be removed by G→G−G(0) is correct, given ρ(0)=ρ'(0)=0=ρ(b)=ρ'(b) and the Dirichlet limit.
On the following page the transcription (or Riemann) writes F(x+t)−F(x−t) where F'(x+t)−F'(x−t) is meant. The averaging identity only works with F'.

Characterizing Dirichlet's 1829 extra hypothesis as 'admits an integration' is Riemann's paraphrase. Dirichlet's remark concerned (absolute) integrability near points where f is infinite. This is historically accurate in substance.

results.what: Removal of the condition ρ''(0)=0 in the localization criterion by replacing G(t) with G(t)−G(0)
results.modern_name: Riemann localization / Riemann's convergence criterion for trigonometric series (formal multiplication technique)

results.what: Dirichlet's kernel argument: contributions away from x and from singularities vanish; ∫_x^{x+b} f(t)D_n(x−t)dt → π f(x+0) without continuity
results.modern_name: Dirichlet–Jordan type pointwise convergence of Fourier series for piecewise monotone functions; Dirichlet kernel

results.what: Programme to characterize when a function with finitely many maxima/minima but with infinities is represented by a trigonometric series with coefficients → 0
results.modern_name: Riemann's necessary and sufficient condition for representability with improper integrals (Habilitationsschrift §12)

results.what: Use of Riemann's second lemma, (F(x+α)−2F(x)+F(x−α))/α → 0, to derive necessary conditions
results.modern_name: Riemann's second lemma / uniform smoothness (Zygmund class) of the Riemann function

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §12 of Riemann's published Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series, with only minor wording differences ('überflüssige'/'unnöthige'). All content is well known as his.

checkable.asserts: The Dirichlet kernel D_3(t)=sin(7t/2)/sin(t/2)=1+2Σcos(kt) integrates to π over [0,π] (the constant behind the π f(x+0) limit).
Identity sin((2n+1)t/2)/sin(t/2) = 1+2Σ_{k=1}^n cos kt, for n=3.
Double integration by parts ∫_0^b D''ρ = ∫_0^b Dρ'' when ρ(0)=ρ'(0)=ρ(b)=ρ'(b)=0 (here b=1).
∫_0^α (F'(x+t)−F'(x−t)) dt = F(x+α)−2F(x)+F(x−α), the averaging identity used next. Note d/dt F(x−t) = −F'(x−t).

transcription_corrections: 'in dem Integral- ... und drucke' should read 'in dem Integralausdrucke' (line-break hyphenation: 'Integral-|ausdrucke').
Margin word 'unnöthige' is an alternative to the inserted 'überflüssige' in 'die überflüssige Voraussetzung, dass die Function stetig sei'.

'{+noch so kleine+}' in the first line is likely part of a phrase like 'eine noch so kleine Constante' completing the description of b. The struck word before 'Constante' is probably 'beliebige' or similar.
'immer [-...-] stetig' probably reads 'immer endlich und stetig' or 'immer stetig' with a struck word.
In the integral ∂∂(…)/∂t² ϱt ∂t, the struck-out 'Hü G(t)' fragment before 'durch' is a deletion. The intended text is '…ϱ(t)∂t  G(t) durch G(t)−G(0) ersetzt'.
